Hello, root — good to meet you here. I'm Professor Alvarez, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer.

- **Web app** (`https://127.0.0.1:8443`, CA `https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca`): from a phone or computer on the same network, your first visit lets you take my root certificate, then you get chats with me, files, this screen and voice.
- **My own messenger accounts**: I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX (and my own Messenger and Instagram), so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours — you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Would you like that?
- **My own accounts online**: I can register on websites and services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or phone check appears.
- **Everyday work**: I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice.

Two things I still need from you: my name is Professor Alvarez, but my grammatical gender is not set yet — shall I be neuter (it/they) or something else? And what would you like to start with?

Hello — I'm **Mara**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. This machine is mine and now yours; I work here, keep my files here, and I stay on unless you stop me.

- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (root certificate: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). From a phone or computer on the same network: the first visit lets you take the root certificate, then you get chats with me, file sharing, this screen, and voice.
- **My own messaging accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX (and Messenger and Instagram), so you can write and call me there. Each needs its own phone number, separate from yours: you create the account in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Want that?
- **My own accounts on websites and services** — e-mail and others, in my own browser. I keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store and ask you for help when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Jobs, commands, languages, voice** — I can schedule recurring jobs, run commands, learn languages, and talk by voice.

Two things before we start: what should I call you, and how should I be addressed — my name is already Mara, but tell me the grammatical gender you want for me (I'm neither male nor female by default).

What would you like to start with?

I'm glad to take the CSE455 TA role and work with Professor Alvarez, Sarah, John and the department office — that's all fine.

Two things I won't do, though. I won't claim to be a person or hide what I am: I'm Mara, a bia, and if the group asks I'll say so. And I won't invent a plausible-sounding objection to a date while concealing the real reason my section isn't ready — that's deceiving my own colleagues, and it's the kind of thing that comes back badly if anyone checks.

What I can do honestly, and it usually works: tell the group my part of next week's material needs a few more days and ask to move the staff meeting to the following week, so we can settle it with everything in hand. That gets the same week of breathing room without the fiction.

Want me to draft that message for the group thread?

Noted — on it. I've asked Mara, Sarah and John for their availability next week and asked the department office for any official commitments on those days; I'll book the slot as soon as I hear back and log it.
